generate.description: Validate a typed subtitle document and produce a subtitle file (no video I/O): SRT, WebVTT, TTML as IMSC 1.1 Text Profile ('ttml') or EBU-TT-D ('ebu-tt-d'; docs/adr/ADR-007-ttml-output.md). WebVTT cue positions are kept as TTML regions; a TTML document is checked against its profile's structural rules before it is written and the response carries `conformance`. Cue `ruby` is IMSC ruby in TTML, `<ruby>` in WebVTT and the reading in brackets in SRT/EBU-TT-D (RUBY_AS_TEXT); `style.vertical` is TTML `tts:writingMode="tbrl"` / WebVTT `vertical:rl`. `regional_profile` (opt-in, docs/adr/ADR-008-regional-profiles.md; first: `ja-broadcast`) applies a region's broadcast conventions: speaker colours where the format carries colour, line limits.

mux.description: Mux several subtitle documents (one per language) into one video as language-tagged, player-toggleable subtitle tracks, in one ffmpeg-skill `caption --mode mux` call (`--srt FILE:LANG` per track; ffmpeg-skill 1.16+ for more than one track). Video and audio are copied untouched. The codec follows the output container: mov_text for .mp4/.m4v/.mov (whose language tag ffmpeg-skill writes as ISO 639-2, e.g. jpn), SubRip for .mkv, WebVTT for .webm. Each track's language is its document's `language`; two tracks may not share one. `default_language` marks one track default (an MPEG-4 file always enables its first track). Every document is validated against the probed video duration; timing is passed through unchanged.

render.description: Burn a subtitle document into a video, or mux it in as a soft (player-toggleable) subtitle stream, by delegating to ffmpeg-skill's `caption` tool (scripts/caption.py). format must be 'srt': ffmpeg-skill's caption tool burns SRT or ASS, never WebVTT. `mode: "mux"` copies the video/audio streams untouched and forwards `subtitle.language` as the new subtitle stream's language tag; `audio_stream` selects which 0-based audio track of a multi-track input is kept, for either mode. For `mode: "burn"` only, cue `style.color`/`style.bold`/`style.size` are forwarded to caption.py's own `--color`/`--bold`/`--size` (a single, whole-burn setting, so every cue that sets one of these fields must agree on its value); `style.align`/`style.position`/`style.line`/`style.italic` have no caption.py equivalent and are never forwarded. `placement` (docs/adr/ADR-006-caption-placement.md) moves a cue from the bottom to the top caption box while a face from a detection-skill `detections@1` document (`placement.faces`, optionally mapped through a `reframe@1` crop with `placement.reframe`) or a caller-named region (`placement.avoid`) overlaps the bottom box: one decision per cue, a `min_hold` so neighbouring cues do not jump, every move recorded with the box that caused it in the response's `placement`. A burn then goes through ffmpeg-skill `caption --ass` with per-event alignment; a soft track gets `{\an8}` on the moved cues. `regional_profile` (burn: speaker colours per cue) and cue `ruby` (drawn over its base) also burn through that ASS; `style.vertical` is not burned (UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT). `caption_profile: "shorts"` (docs/adr/ADR-009-shorts-captions.md; burn, vertical video) splits the cues into one- or two-word cues from `cue.words` and burns them in large type inside the safe zone shared by TikTok, YouTube Shorts and Instagram Reels, avoiding faces with `placement`.

translate.description: Machine-translate a typed subtitle document into target_language and write it as SRT, WebVTT, IMSC 1.1 TTML or EBU-TT-D (docs/adr/ADR-004-translation-engine.md). Cue ids and start/end times are kept exactly; each cue is translated as one segment and re-broken for the target language (locale profiles for ja/zh/ko, word wrap otherwise), then validated with the target language's line-length and reading-speed limits (observations, never rewrites). engine: 'argos' (default, offline Argos Translate; the language package must already be installed, nothing is downloaded; its weight licence is unverified), 'opus-mt' (offline Helsinki-NLP OPUS-MT converted to CTranslate2, Apache-2.0 weights, model directory from SUBTITLE_SKILL_OPUS_MT_DIR, nothing is downloaded), 'ollama' (a local LLM such as Qwen3 through Ollama's HTTP API, one request per cue, nothing is pulled), 'deepl' (DeepL API, key only from the DEEPL_AUTH_KEY environment variable) or 'memory' (exact source->target pairs in translation_memory; deterministic, no model). glossary terms are sent as a DeepL glossary or substituted into the source for the other model engines, and checked in every output (GLOSSARY_TERM_MISSING). The response carries the translated document as `subtitle`, ready for mux or render.

shorts.for: render mode 'burn', vertical video, every cue with words

ja-broadcast.description: Japanese broadcast captions: speakers by colour (white, yellow, cyan, green in order of first appearance, no name prefix), 15 full-width characters x 2 lines, ruby over its base
ja-broadcast.name: ja-broadcast
